name: Israel's Collapsing Shell of Dust
description: A thin spherical shell of dust falling under its own weight, with flat spacetime inside it and Schwarzschild's vacuum outside. Werner Israel solved its motion in 1966 with the junction conditions he wrote for a surface that carries matter. The event horizon forms at the centre of the flat interior before the shell arrives.
convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and we keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: How little can you build a black hole from? The classic recipe, J. Robert Oppenheimer and Hartland Snyder's of 1939, takes a whole ball of dust, a piece of a closed universe falling in on itself [oppenheimersnyder1939]. Now blow the ball out into a bubble: all of the dust on one thin sphere, and nothing inside. Inside the bubble spacetime is flat, outside it the field is Karl Schwarzschild's, and all of the matter is on the bubble [schwarzschild1916, poisson2004]. How it falls is a problem Werner Israel settled in 1966 [israel1966].¶The trouble is the seam: on the shell the metric has a crease, and Einstein's equations put a sheet of matter there with no thickness [poisson2004]. Such sheets go back to the early 1920s, to Kornel Lanczos and Nikhilranjan Sen, and the geometric conditions for joining two spacetimes along a surface to Georges Darmois in 1927 [lanczos1924shell, sen1924, darmois1927, mansouri1996]. The junction conditions of the 1950s, those of S. O'Brien and John Lighton Synge among them, amount to asking for coordinates that are continuous across the surface [mansouri1996]. Israel had been Synge's student in Dublin, and since 1958 he had taught mathematics at the University of Alberta [kamal2008].¶In his paper Israel threw the coordinates out. The histories of such surfaces, he wrote, "are characterized in a purely geometrical way by the extrinsic curvatures of their imbeddings in space-time", and "no mention of « admissible » or, indeed, any space-time co-ordinates is needed" [israel1966]. Each side keeps the coordinates that suit it, the two sides must agree on the geometry of the surface itself, and the jump in how the surface bends from one side to the other is the matter sitting on it [israel1966, poisson2004]. In 1996 R. Mansouri and M. Khorrami wrote that the method "has found its final formulation in the outstanding paper of Israel", and they called the conditions by the names of Darmois and Israel together [mansouri1996].¶For a shell of dust of rest mass $m$ the conditions come down to one line, $M = m\sqrt{1 + \dot{R}^2/c^2} - Gm^2/2c^2R$, where $R$ is the shell's radius, $\dot{R} = dR/d\tau$ is its rate of change on the dust's own clock, and $M$ is the mass in Schwarzschild's metric outside [israel1966, poisson2004]. The first term is the dust's energy of motion, rest mass included, and the second is the binding energy of the shell, so a shell at rest weighs less from outside than its dust does [poisson2004]. A shell with $M < m$ turns back at $R = Gm^2/2c^2(m - M)$, and one with $M = m$ falls from rest at infinity [poisson2004]. Schwarzschild's own time runs to infinity before the shell reaches $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, while the advanced time of Arthur Eddington and David Finkelstein follows it through the horizon to the centre [schwarzschild1916, eddington1924, finkelstein1958]. Take the rest mass away and the shell is one of light, which R. J. Adler, J. D. Bjorken, P. Chen, and J. S. Liu called "the simplest complete example of gravitational collapse" [adler2005].¶What happens when the shell reaches the centre? Israel took that up in a second paper, sent off from the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies in May 1966, "on the hypothesis that the shell rebounds elastically after imploding to a point" [israel1967collapse]. "The resulting description involves certain causal anomalies", he reported [israel1967collapse]. He gave reasons for believing that a real collapse "does not proceed irreversibly to zero volume, but is an oscillatory phenomenon", and that near its smallest size a region develops "where past and future cannot be globally distinguished" [israel1967collapse]. With V. de la Cruz he then gave the shell a charge and a charged body at its centre, and got a true bounce "at a nonzero minimal radius", possible "even after the shell has collapsed inside the Schwarzschild sphere" [delacruz1967].¶Others kept the shell and gave it charge: can enough of it stop the fall? Karel Kuchař's answer of 1968 was that "no charge, however high it may be, can stop the gravitational collapse of the shell below the upper Nordström radius" [kuchar1968]. For David Boulware's charged shell of 1973 the verdict was that it "can collapse to form a naked singularity if, and only if, the matter energy density of the shell is negative" [boulware1973]. In the quantum version that Petr Hájíček, Bernard Kay, and Kuchař solved in 1992, "a special choice of the time variable" makes the shell's equations those of "a charged relativistic particle moving radially in an external Coulomb potential", and "precisely the same amount of probability and energy comes out as was sent in" [hajicek1992]. The junction conditions went on to other shells that stay where they are put, at the throat of Matt Visser's wormhole and on the skin of the gravastar [visser1989nuclphysb, visser2004].

related.text: The outside of the shell. The mass in it is the energy of the shell, the dust's energy of motion less the binding energy [poisson2004].
The inside of the shell, flat until the shell arrives. The event horizon starts at its centre and crosses it at the speed of light.
The collapse of a whole ball of dust, with a piece of a closed universe inside where the shell has flat space [oppenheimersnyder1939].
The shell of light, the limit $m \to 0$ of the shell of dust at fixed $M$, which falls along one ingoing ray [adler2005].
Two Schwarzschild exteriors joined at a throat by the same junction conditions, on a shell of negative energy density [visser1989nuclphysb].
A shell that stays put, with de Sitter space inside it where the falling shell has flat space [visser2004].
Israel's shell given a charge, with Reissner-Nordström's field outside. With more charge than rest mass it turns round inside the inner horizon and leaves into another exterior [delacruz1967].
The same collapse made of light, which Haggard and Rovelli let bounce and come back out through a white hole [haggard2015fireworks].

coordinates.name: Flat Interior

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass $M$ measured outside the shell, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Rest mass $m$ of the dust as a length, $\mu = Gm/c^2$; a shell with $\mu = r_s/2$ falls from rest at infinity, and a heavier one from rest at a finite radius
Areal radius of the shell, a length. With $\tau$ the proper time of the dust and $\gamma = r_s/2\mu + \mu/2R$, it falls as $dR/d(c\tau) = -\sqrt{\gamma^2 - 1}$ while $dT/d\tau = \gamma$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, r, \theta, \phi)$ inside the shell, with $T$ the time of an observer at rest at the centre, carrying dimensions of time, and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Schwarzschild Exterior

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass $M$ measured outside the shell, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Rest mass $m$ of the dust as a length, $\mu = Gm/c^2$; a shell with $\mu = r_s/2$ falls from rest at infinity, and a heavier one from rest at a finite radius

Areal radius of the shell, a length. With $\tau$ the proper time of the dust and $\beta = r_s/2\mu - \mu/2R$, it falls as $dR/d(c\tau) = -\sqrt{\beta^2 - 1 + r_s/R}$ while $(1 - r_s/R)\,dt/d\tau = \beta$, and it reaches $r_s$ only as $t \to \infty$

coordinates.convention: We use Schwarzschild coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ outside the shell, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius, the same $r$ as inside. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein Exterior

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius of the mass $M$ measured outside the shell, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$
Rest mass $m$ of the dust as a length, $\mu = Gm/c^2$; a shell with $\mu = r_s/2$ falls from rest at infinity, and a heavier one from rest at a finite radius

Areal radius of the shell, a length. With $\tau$ the proper time of the dust and $\beta = r_s/2\mu - \mu/2R$, it falls as $dR/d(c\tau) = -\sqrt{\beta^2 - 1 + r_s/R}$ while $dv/d(c\tau) = 1/\left(\beta + \sqrt{\beta^2 - 1 + r_s/R}\right)$, through $r_s$ to $R = 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$ outside the shell, with the advanced time $v = ct + r + r_s\ln\left|r/r_s - 1\right|$ a length, constant along ingoing light rays, and $r$ the areal radius. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
